column1: # Git Author/Committer Mapping Template
# This CSV file is used by scripts/rewrite-authors.sh to rewrite Git history
# changing author and committer identities across all commits.
# IMPORTANT: This operation rewrites Git history. Use with caution!
# CSV FORMAT:
# The CSV must contain the following 8 columns in this exact order:
#   1. author_name_from      - Original author name to match (case-sensitive)
#   2. committer_name_from   - Original committer name to match (case-sensitive)
#   3. author_email_from     - Original author email to match (case-sensitive)
#   4. committer_email_from  - Original committer email to match (case-sensitive)
#   5. author_name_to        - New author name (what it should become)
#   6. committer_name_to     - New committer name (what it should become)
#   7. author_email_to       - New author email (what it should become)
#   8. committer_email_to    - New committer email (what it should become)
# FIELD FORMAT RULES:
# - Names: Can contain letters
#          Examples: "John Doe"
# - Emails: Must be valid email format (user@domain.tld)
#          Examples: "user@example.com"
# - Whitespace: Leading/trailing spaces in fields are automatically trimmed
# - Special Characters: If a field contains commas
#                      Examples: "Doe
# - Quote Escaping: To include a quote in a quoted field
#                  Example: "John ""The Dev"" Doe"
# - Empty Fields: Not recommended
# COMMON SCENARIOS:
# 1. Name Change Only: Change name but keep same email
#    Use case: Developer changed their display name
# 2. Email Change Only: Keep same name but change email
#    Use case: Developer changed companies or email addresses
# 3. Full Identity Change: Change both name and email
#    Use case: Correct misattributed commits or merge duplicate identities
# 4. Normalize Variations: Map multiple variations to a single canonical identity
#    Use case: Same person used different name spellings or email addresses
# TIPS:
# - Run "git log --all --format='%an <%ae> | %cn <%ce>'" to see all current identities
# - Run "git shortlog -sne --all" to see author statistics
# - Use scripts/verify-authors.sh after rewriting to verify the changes
# - Test with --dry-run flag first: scripts/rewrite-authors.sh --dry-run mapping.csv
# - Create a backup before running: the script does this automatically
# - In most cases
